added_models.model: Rhesus monkey PK/PD and repeat-dose toxicology (somatrogon)

engagement.note: Somatrogon every 5 days gave exposure comparable to daily rhGH and raised IGF-1 in rats and rhesus monkeys.
engagement.quote: Repeated administration of MOD-4023 led to elevated levels of insulin-like growth factor 1 (IGF-1), and twice-weekly injections of MOD-4023 resulted in larger increase in weight gain with fewer injections and a lower accumulative hGH dose.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract only (paywalled Mol Pharm); opening entry at publication (epub 2016-01-18), though the studies preceded first-in-human dosing (NCT01060722, started 2009-10).
engagement.judgement: Monkey kept as its own track: the draft's hypox-rat track is somatrogon's rat system; the monkey is a separate species with its own IGF-1 readout.

engagement.note: Weekly somatrogon raised IGF-1 dose-dependently in GH-deficient adults and held IGF-1 SDS in the normal range, as in monkeys.
engagement.short: GHD adults IGF-1 up, as monkey
engagement.quote: Dose-dependent response was observed for both PK and PD data of weekly MOD-4023 treatment. Insulin-like growth factor I (IGF-I) SDS levels were maintained within normal range.
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract read (PMC5292974 available, full text not read). Adult phase 2 NCT01225666 has no posted results; epub 2016-12-08.
engagement.reason: IGF-1 rose in GHD adults, as monkeys
engagement.judgement: Paired by me: Strasburger does not set the monkey data beside patients in the abstract. Monkey predicted IGF-1 rise on infrequent dosing; adults showed it on weekly dosing, so same in direction.

dose.note: Monkey and rat exposure was matched to daily rhGH per 5 days; no human dose, exposure target or margin stated in the abstract.
dose.quote: administration of MOD-4023 every 5 days in rats and monkeys resulted in exposure comparable to daily rhGH, and the serum half-life of MOD-4023 was significantly longer.
dose.confidence_note: Abstract only; the full text may state a human dose projection that was not checked.
dose.reason: No human dose or margin stated
dose.judgement: An animal-to-animal exposure comparison is not a human dose prediction; children later needed 0.66 mg/kg/wk (Zelinska 2017), but no monkey target to score it against.

safety.note: Repeat-dose toxicology called somatrogon well tolerated in rats and monkeys; no harm named. Pediatric lipoatrophy case reports followed in 2025.
safety.quote: MOD-4023 was found to be well-tolerated in rats and monkeys, with minimal adverse events, suggesting an acceptable safety profile.
safety.confidence_note: Abstract only; whether the monkey studies examined injection-site lipoatrophy is not known. Toxicology detail and FDA/EMA nonclinical reviews not checked.
safety.judgement: A general tolerability statement names no harm, so no_prediction. The 2025 lipoatrophy case series (3 GHD children, no denominator; rhGH also causes it) is not scored as a contra of a silence that is unpublished in detail.

considered_not_added: Somatrogon rats in Hershkovitz 2016 (Sprague-Dawley PK/tox, weight gain): same rat system as the draft's hypox-rat-gh track (Fares 2010), not a new track.
Somatropin pegol (NNC126-0083) preclinical models: no published nonclinical source found; only phase 1 healthy-volunteer (2010), GHD adult (2011) and GHD child (2011) trials.
Somavaratan (VRS-317) own models: rats, juvenile monkeys and pig/monkey lipoatrophy already tracked; no PK/PD or QSP model found.

Somatrogon population PK / IGF-1 PK/PD models (OR10-04 2020; Stan/Torsten popPK 2025; IGF-1 assessment 2025): built from patient data to interpret IGF-1 sampling, not a model prediction compared with a later patient result.

Somatrogon lipoatrophy case reports (10.4274/jcrpe.galenos.2025.2025-10-16, GHD; 10.3390/children12010058, idiopathic short stature, outside population): no denominator; noted on the monkey safety entry, not scored.
Somatrogon FDA BLA 761184 / EMA Ngenla EPAR nonclinical reviews: not in the source bundle and not fetched within budget; model_filed left null.
Patient-derived cells, ex-vivo sensitivity, PDX, human challenge or genetic models (e.g. GHR-deficient Laron patients) for these drugs: none found compared with clinical response.
